verdict: Zimmer Biomet grew sales 3% to $2.1B on upper-single-digit growth in hips, extremities and surgical products, but GAAP profit fell 17% as an acquisition-related credit a year ago swung to a cost and spending rose.

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: flat vs a year ago, excluding amortization and one-off items

segments.name: Knees
segments.note: Knee replacement implants — Zimmer Biomet's largest category. Sales fell 3%, with the U.S. down 2% and international down 5%.

segments.name: S.E.T.
segments.note: Sports medicine, extremities and trauma — including the Paragon 28 foot-and-ankle business bought in April 2025. Sales rose 7%.

segments.name: Hips
segments.note: Hip replacement implants. Sales rose 6%, up 6% in the U.S. and 6% internationally.

segments.name: Technology & Data, Bone Cement and Surgical
segments.note: Surgical tools, bone cement and data/technology products — the smallest category and the fastest growing, up 12%.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: The sales force that works with surgeons and hospitals, plus head-office costs.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands, patents and customer relationships bought in past acquisitions, year by year.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing and testing new implants and surgical products.

opex.name: Acquisition, integration and divestiture
opex.note: Deal and integration costs — a year ago this line was a $34M credit, so the swing cost about $54M year over year.

opex.name: Restructuring and other cost reduction
opex.note: Severance and program costs from cost-cutting initiatives.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $75M plus $3M of other expense, net (rounded from $2.5M), and $1M of the quarter's earnings belongs to noncontrolling interests — so net income here is the $192M attributable to Zimmer Biomet shareholders (printed: $191.6M; consolidated net earnings were $192.9M).
oneTimers: Acquisition, integration and divestiture swung from a $34M credit a year ago to a $20M cost — a roughly $54M year-over-year drag on operating profit.
Restructuring and cost-reduction charges were $14M in the quarter.
Adjusted net earnings were $363M versus $192M GAAP — the gap is mostly the $166M of intangible amortization plus restructuring and deal costs that Zimmer Biomet excludes from its adjusted figures.

takeaways.title: Growth outside knees
takeaways.text: Hips grew 6%, S.E.T. 7% and Technology & Data, Bone Cement and Surgical 12% — together two-thirds of sales — while Knees, still the biggest category, fell 3%.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS held flat
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS of $1.90 matched last year even as GAAP EPS fell to $1.00, because the adjusted figure strips out $166M of acquisition amortization and the deal-cost swing.

takeaways.title: Cash flow stayed strong
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $560M and free cash flow $372M in the quarter, even though GAAP net earnings fell 17% to $192M.

footerNote: Zimmer Biomet prints its 10-Q figures in tenths of a million (net sales $2,062.9M; cost of products sold $594.5M; operating profit $307.6M). This chart rounds each line to the nearest $M, so individual lines can differ by $1M from a simple rounding of the printed totals. Product categories are the four printed in the release — Knees $767.5M, Hips $536.5M, S.E.T. $578.3M and Technology & Data, Bone Cement and Surgical $180.6M before rounding.
